bull.b: The Phase 1 ALLOHA results provide an encouraging clinical signal for TSC-101, with complete donor chimerism across all currently tracked Cohort C patients and generally favorable safety. This supports the underlying therapeutic potential even though development has been reprioritized.

Material cost savings and a projected cash runway into the fourth quarter of 2027 give TScan more time to advance its prioritized solid-tumor programs. Greater financial durability can reduce near-term funding pressure and support milestone execution after the restructuring.

A high latest-period gross margin indicates that direct costs are not the main constraint on TScan’s economics. If maintained as programs progress, this profile could allow future collaboration or product revenue to contribute meaningfully before operating expenses are fully scaled.

bear.b: The declining TTM revenue base and continuing large operating and net losses show that TScan has not established a self-sustaining commercial or collaboration revenue engine. Persistent losses increase dependence on external financing and make future development progress more financially constrained.

Ongoing negative operating and free cash flow indicate that the business continues to consume capital, while rising debt-to-equity reflects a shrinking equity base and greater leverage. Together, these trends reduce financial flexibility and can complicate funding of the pipeline.

The Amgen termination weakens TScan’s partnership-driven revenue model by eliminating expected future milestone and royalty opportunities from the collaboration. It also reduces external validation and potential non-dilutive funding support for the company’s discovery platform.
